regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters on the headline; IIP overall came in at 6.7% YoY, down from 8.8%, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The quality question: PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slipped to 52.8 — the goods economy is losing the baton precisely as capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity signals the investment cycle should be self-sustaining. The inversion: if private capex is genuinely firing, why is core sector growth decelerating for the second consecutive month?","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY looks manageable until you decompose it — fuel at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, up from 20.05%) is doing the heavy lifting upward, while core CPI at 3.9% YoY remains relatively contained at the 28th percentile. The gap between fuel and core is the trap: RBI's own inflation forecast has already been revised to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%, signalling the MPC knows the headline will worsen. WPI at 9.92% YoY means producer margins are being squeezed — that feeds into core CPI with a two-quarter lag.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY — a 630 bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81.4%, the 75th percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was the pre-taper tantrum period of FY13-14; within 12 months, emergency rate action followed. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding demand is rising precisely as the deposit base thins — the regulator's next move on risk weights is not a question of if, but when.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY leaves the real rate at approximately 80 bps — thin cover for an economy with fuel inflation at a 95th-percentile print and INR at 97.09, its weakest level in the dataset. The RBI is threading a needle: cut and the INR breaks further, importing more inflation; hold and credit costs stay elevated, compressing capex IRRs. The second-order effect of INR weakness is the one the market is underpricing — every 3% depreciation adds roughly 15-20 bps to imported inflation with a two-quarter lag.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity from 75.6% — the 74th percentile — is the most credible signal that the private investment cycle has genuine momentum. At 77-78% utilisation, the historical trigger for greenfield capex decisions activates; we are at that threshold. The contradiction: core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0%) suggests the upstream infrastructure feeding this capex cycle is moderating. Home loan disbursements at ₹19,930 cr / quarter, up from ₹15,914 cr, confirm residential capex is also accelerating — but at an average loan rate of 7.25% p.a. that is still historically elevated.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but the composition matters more than the headline — passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY suggest both urban discretionary and rural mass-market demand are holding. The inversion: GST growth at this level partly reflects formalisation reclassifying existing informal spend, not purely new demand creation. Credit card growth at just 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) is the quiet signal that urban discretionary credit appetite is softening even as vehicle sales look robust — watch this divergence for the first sign of consumption fatigue.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Industry credit at 20% YoY and services credit at 22.9% YoY are outpacing deposit mobilisation.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (at 0th percentile, a structural low) suggests corporates are rationing debt — a warning sign of credit stress ahead.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically tight. The last time divergence this wide persisted, RBI cut rates within 90 days and NBFC spreads widened 150+ bps.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month, 74th percentile) is at the inflection point where capex becomes self-reinforcing. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (78th percentile) and credit to agriculture at 17% YoY (77th percentile) show broad-based investment appetite. Home loan disbursements at ₹19,930 cr / quarter (up from ₹15,914 cr / quarter prior) and average home loan rate declining to 7.25% p.a. (from 7.45% p.a.) indicate residential capex is also accelerating.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% means pricing power is returning — margins will expand before new supply comes online (typically 18-24 month lag). Avoid over-leveraged construction companies; focus on those with strong balance sheets and order books > 2 years. Residential real estate is in early-cycle — builders with land banks in Tier-1 cities will see 20%+ EBITDA growth over next 2 years.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile historically preceded 18-month capex booms. Last time it was this high (2021-22), capex growth sustained at 15%+ for 6 quarters.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Backdoor","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (rising 2 in a row: ₹29,845 → ₹31,961 → ₹32,297), at 92nd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn, 82nd percentile). But SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (rising 2 in a row: ₹16.64 → ₹18.2 → ₹18.62, 93rd percentile) is growing 40% faster than account growth (14% YoY). This means average ticket size per SIP account is rising sharply — affluent investors are using SIP as a tax-efficient vehicle, not mass retail. DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, rising 2 in a row) and FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) confirm institutional money is flooding in. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) and average MF AUM at ₹88.31 lakh cr (88th percentile) both rising 2 in a row.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Affluent retail is front-running institutional money. Reduce equity allocation by 10-15% over next 2 quarters. Rotate from large-cap to mid-cap value (where SIP penetration is lower and valuations are cheaper). Increase allocation to fixed income and gold — SIP AUM growth at 93rd percentile historically precedes 12-18 month equity corrections. Watch for SIP account growth to decelerate; when it does, the flow impulse is exhausted.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile last occurred in 2021 (pre-correction) and 2017 (pre-correction). Average ticket size rising is a structural shift toward affluent participation, not mass retail deepening.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Pause","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior month, 95th percentile) is the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at $104.72 / bbl (rising 5 in a row: $100.5 → $101.1 → $101.1 → $103.8 → $104.4 → $104.7) and WTI at $91.85 / bbl (up 4 of last 5) signal sustained oil strength. Natural gas at $3.22 / MMBtu (up 4 of last 5, 20th percentile) is rising but remains historically cheap. Copper at $6.692 / lb (80th percentile) and iron ore at $161.91 / t (63rd percentile) show broad commodity strength. India's headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY, 41st percentile) and core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile) are both rising. RBI's inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6% YoY prior) signals RBI expects further overshoot.","implication":"RBI's rate pause is at risk if fuel inflation persists above 20% YoY for another month. Expect a 25 bps rate hike in Q2 FY2027 (April-June 2026). Overweight energy stocks and underweight consumer discretionary. Hedge INR weakness — oil imports will widen the current account deficit. Avoid long-duration bonds; yields will rise 30-50 bps if RBI hikes. Commodity-linked stocks (oil, metals) will outperform; avoid import-dependent sectors (auto, pharma).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural shock. Last time it was this high (2022), RBI hiked rates 190 bps in 6 months and INR weakened 8%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Cycle Resumes; Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a. prior, rising 2 in a row, 68th percentile). US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.22% (down from 5.28% prior but at 95th percentile historically, rising 3 of last 5). US CPI at 3.353% YoY (up from 3.3039% YoY, rising 2 in a row) and US core PCE at 3.0076% YoY (up from 2.9835% YoY) signal inflation persistence. US GDP SAAR at 2.2% (up from 2.5% prior, 50th percentile) is moderating. US PMI composite at 56 index (up from 54.5, 84th percentile) shows US economy still strong. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a., 86th percentile) signals BoJ tightening. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% p.a., 59th percentile). DXY at 102.231 index (56th percentile, up 3 of last 5) shows dollar strength. Global PMI composite at 53.5 index (82nd percentile).","implication":"Carry trades are unwinding. INR weakness (97.09 ₹ / USD, 94th percentile, up 4 of last 5) will accelerate if Fed stays higher for longer. Reduce leverage in emerging market positions. Overweight USD-denominated assets and underweight INR-denominated assets. Expect 2-3% INR depreciation over next 6 months. Avoid long-duration EM bonds; yields will rise as carry unwinds. US equities (S&P 500 at 100th percentile, Nasdaq at 74th percentile) are expensive but will outperform as capital repatriates from EM.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"US 10-year Treasury at 95th percentile and Fed funds rising is a classic carry unwind signal. Last time this happened (2022), EM currencies fell 8-12% and equity flows reversed.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerating; RBI Intervention Limits","data_text":"INR at 97.09 ₹ / USD (up from 96.78 ₹ / USD prior, up 4 of last 5: 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 97.09, 94th percentile). This is the weakest level in the dataset. DXY at 102.231 index (56th percentile, up 3 of last 5) shows broad dollar strength. FII equity net flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) are positive but volatile (recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631). The reversal from -₹3,111.9 cr net outflow to +₹29,631 cr net inflow in one month suggests FII flows are reactive, not structural. India's household debt at 42.6% of GDP (51st percentile) and corporate debt at 51.9% of GDP (42nd percentile) are moderate, but INR weakness will increase debt servicing costs for corporates with USD liabilities. Gold in INR at ₹13,161 / g (100th percentile, up 4 of last 5) shows INR weakness is real.","implication":"RBI's FX reserves are being deployed to defend INR, but intervention capacity is finite. Expect INR to breach 98 ₹ / USD within 2 months if oil stays above $100 / bbl and FII flows remain volatile. Corporates with USD debt should hedge now — INR forwards are expensive but necessary. Overweight gold and USD-denominated assets. Underweight INR-denominated bonds and equities with high USD debt. Expect RBI to cut rates faster than currently priced to support INR (rate cuts will come before inflation fully moderates).","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"INR at 94th percentile weakness is a structural signal. Last time INR was this weak (2022), RBI cut rates 40 bps despite inflation concerns, and INR continued to weaken for another 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (down from 4.39 mn sq ft / quarter prior, 0th percentile, strong-negative score of -100). This is the lowest in the dataset. Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (up from 13.74%, 41st percentile). But Nifty IT index is flat (Nifty 50 at 22,520.45, 72nd percentile, up 3 of last 5). This disconnect is the signal: traditional IT services companies are NOT the office buyers anymore. Global Capability Centres (GCCs) — captive R&D and engineering centres of multinational corporations — are consolidating into fewer, larger hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune). Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shrinking office footprints as they shift to hybrid and offshore models. Meanwhile, retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5%, 7th percentile, strong-positive score of 86) shows retail real estate is THRIVING. E-commerce GMV growth at 18% YoY (26th percentile, mild-negative score of -24) is slowing, but physical retail is absorbing space. This is a structural shift: office RE is decoupling from IT services; retail RE is decoupling from e-commerce growth.","implication":"SELL office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield all down 15-30% YTD). These are value traps — office absorption will remain weak for 2-3 years as GCCs consolidate and IT services downsize. BUY retail REITs and retail-focused developers — retail is the new growth engine, not a defensive play. Avoid IT services stocks on valuation alone; they are not office buyers anymore. The office collapse is NOT a macro signal; it's a sectoral rotation. Allocate capital to retail, logistics, and data centre REITs instead.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is a structural break, not a cyclical dip. The last time office absorption was this weak (2020 COVID), it took 3 years to recover. This time, recovery may never come — GCC consolidation is permanent.","is_surprise":true}

{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Fuel Spike Corners RBI — Growth Holds, But the Margin Narrows

The facts:

  • GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile) with PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) — but IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, and core sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, up from 20.05% YoY) has forced RBI's own inflation forecast to 5.1% YoY — up 50 bps from its prior 4.6% YoY estimate.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) sits at the historical threshold where private capex decisions activate — IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY confirms the signal.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY coexist with credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) — mass-market volume is holding while urban credit appetite softens.

The tension: The growth composite looks solid, but the fuel-inflation shock is compressing the RBI's room to manoeuvre — a 5.1% YoY inflation forecast against a 5.25% p.a. repo rate leaves a real rate buffer too thin to absorb further crude upside.

Bottom line: Watch Brent: a sustained print above $105/bbl forces RBI's hand on the inflation forecast and effectively closes the rate-cut window for FY27.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Strength, China Contraction — India Caught in the Crossfire

The facts:

  • US PMI composite at 56 (84th percentile) and Fed funds at 3.75% p.a. (rising 2 in a row) signal a US economy that is re-accelerating even as the Fed tightens.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) — down from 5.28% but structurally elevated — is tightening global financial conditions independently of the Fed's policy rate.
  • But China PMI composite at 49.5 (contraction) and GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) remove the commodity-demand floor that would otherwise cap Brent's upside.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) continues unwinding yen carry — DXY at 102.2 (56th percentile) reflects dollar strength that pressures EM currencies including INR.

The tension: US strength is keeping global rates elevated and the dollar bid, while China weakness prevents the commodity-price relief that would ease India's import bill — India faces the worst combination: no export tailwind from China, full oil-price pain from the US demand impulse.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the underappreciated tail risk — a further hike to 1.25% p.a. accelerates yen carry unwind and triggers EM capital outflows within 30-60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — But Built on a Thinning Deposit Base

The facts:

  • DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, rising 2 in a row) are absorbing supply that FII flows — volatile at ₹29,631 cr net / month after a prior month outflow of ₹3,112 cr — cannot be relied upon to provide.
  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising 2 in a row) with SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) growing 40% faster than account growth — average ticket size is rising, signalling affluent capital, not mass retail.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit growth of 17.1% YoY means the same household savings flowing into MFs are not flowing into bank deposits — the CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) is a direct consequence.
  • Corp bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile) is at its lowest in the dataset — corporates are not tapping bond markets, amplifying pressure on bank credit.

The tension: Record mutual fund and DII flows create an illusion of liquidity abundance, but the underlying deposit base is thinning — the financial system is rotating savings from banks to markets faster than the credit cycle can safely absorb.

Bottom line: If deposit growth does not recover to 13%+ YoY within two quarters, expect RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights for unsecured and NBFC lending.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Lifts Premium Housing — Office REITs Price a Structural Shift

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Premium segment (₹80 lakh – ₹1.5 cr) commands 34% of launch supply; Hyderabad leads sales momentum at 15% YoY with launches surging 120% YoY — but 29 months of unsold inventory is a supply overhang that NRI demand alone cannot clear.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile) — GCCs now 41% of occupier mix vs IT services at 15% — explains why Embassy REIT trades at ₹370/unit (down from ₹431) and Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹494).
  • But retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile) shows physical retail is the structural winner — e-commerce GMV growth at 18% YoY (26th percentile) is not cannibalising mall space.

The tension: Office REITs are repricing a structural demand shift — GCC consolidation into fewer hubs compresses aggregate absorption even as city-level leasing in Hyderabad (+47% YoY) and NCR (+106% YoY) looks strong; the REIT index reflects the aggregate, not the city winners.

Bottom line: Avoid office REIT index exposure; prefer direct city-level plays in Hyderabad and NCR where GCC-led leasing is accelerating, and watch Hyderabad unsold inventory (29 months) as the price-correction trigger.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Crude Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent rising 5 sessions straight to $104.72/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widening CAD by ~40 bps and feeding CPI with a 2-quarter lag.
  • INR at 97.09 ₹/USD (94th percentile, weakest in dataset, up 4 of last 5 sessions) — gold in INR at ₹13,161/g (100th percentile) confirms the depreciation is real, not statistical.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) with credit growing at 17.1% YoY vs deposits at 10.8% YoY — NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding stress is building.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — further tightening triggers yen carry unwind, pressuring EM flows; FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month reversed from a prior outflow of ₹3,112 cr, signalling reactive rather than structural positioning.

The tension: All four risks share a common amplifier: a Brent print above $110/bbl simultaneously widens CAD, breaks INR through 99, forces RBI to abandon its pause, and triggers FII outflows — the feedback loop is tighter than the individual risk scores suggest.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a close above $107/bbl is the threshold that forces RBI's inflation forecast above 5.5% YoY and effectively ends the rate-pause narrative.

"}
